checks.title: Agent context file present (AGENTS.md)
checks.evidence: No AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or GEMINI.md at repository root, and no .claude/CLAUDE.md or .claude/AGENTS.md project instructions.
checks.remediation: Create an AGENTS.md at the repository root describing what the project is, how to build/test it, and the conventions agents must follow.

checks.title: Agent context file is substantive
checks.evidence: No agent context file to evaluate.
checks.remediation: Flesh out AGENTS.md: add sections for project overview, build & test commands, architecture, and conventions (aim for 20+ meaningful lines with headings).

checks.title: Scoped rules in use
checks.evidence: Found 1 rule(s) (claude-code): examples/CLAUDE.md
checks.remediation: Add at least one scoped rule file for your AI tool (e.g. .cursor/rules/*.mdc, .windsurf/rules/*.md, .clinerules/*.md, .claude/rules/*.md) or a nested AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md in a subdirectory, stating the project non-negotiables.

checks.title: Rules have valid frontmatter
checks.evidence: All 1 rule(s) declare usable frontmatter.
checks.remediation: Give every rule activation metadata in frontmatter (description, globs/trigger/paths/applyTo, or alwaysApply) so the agent knows when to load it.

checks.title: Rules are scoped, not all always-on
checks.evidence: 1 rule(s): 1 path-scoped, 0 always-on.
checks.remediation: Scope rules to paths (globs, trigger glob, paths, applyTo) instead of making everything always-on — blanket rules consume context on every request.

checks.title: No bloated rules (≤500 lines each)
checks.evidence: All 1 rule(s) are ≤500 lines.
checks.remediation: Split rules longer than 500 lines into focused, scoped rules or move procedural content into a skill — huge rules crowd out task context.

checks.title: README present
checks.evidence: README.md found at repository root.
checks.remediation: Add a README.md — agents (and humans) use it as the first orientation document.

checks.title: No legacy .cursorrules file
checks.evidence: No deprecated .cursorrules file.
checks.remediation: Migrate the legacy .cursorrules file to scoped rules with frontmatter (.cursor/rules/*.mdc or your tool equivalent) — .cursorrules is deprecated.

checks.title: At least one agent skill defined
checks.evidence: Found 11 skill(s) (claude-code): skills/backend-patterns/SKILL.md, skills/clickhouse-io/SKILL.md, skills/coding-standards/SKILL.md, …
checks.remediation: Create a SKILL.md under your tool skills directory (.cursor/skills/, .claude/skills/, .devin/skills/, or .agents/skills/) packaging a procedural workflow the agent should follow on demand.

checks.title: Skills declare name and description
checks.evidence: Skills missing name/description frontmatter: skills/eval-harness/SKILL.md, skills/project-guidelines-example/SKILL.md, skills/verification-loop/SKILL.md
checks.remediation: Add frontmatter with name: and description: to every SKILL.md — the agent decides whether to load a skill from those two fields alone.

checks.title: Explicit workflows/commands defined
checks.evidence: Found 15 command/workflow(s) (claude-code): commands/build-fix.md, commands/checkpoint.md, commands/code-review.md, …
checks.remediation: Add explicit workflow/command entry points (.cursor/commands/, .windsurf/workflows/, .claude/commands/, .continue/prompts/, …) for workflows you trigger intentionally.

checks.title: Skill descriptions are trigger-worthy
checks.evidence: Skills with short/missing descriptions: skills/eval-harness/SKILL.md, skills/project-guidelines-example/SKILL.md, skills/verification-loop/SKILL.md
checks.remediation: Write skill descriptions of 40+ characters that say when to use the skill ("Use when…"), not just what it is — vague descriptions never trigger.

checks.title: Custom subagent defined
checks.evidence: Found 9 subagent(s) (claude-code): agents/architect.md, agents/build-error-resolver.md, agents/code-reviewer.md, …
checks.remediation: Create a subagent definition (.cursor/agents/, .claude/agents/, or .opencode/agents/) for a purpose-built delegate (planning, review, release…).

checks.title: Subagents declare name and description
checks.evidence: All 9 subagent(s) declare name and description.
checks.remediation: Add frontmatter with name: and description: to every subagent definition — the parent agent decides whether to delegate from those two fields alone.

checks.title: Hooks configuration present and valid JSON
checks.evidence: hooks/hooks.json contains a parseable hooks configuration.
checks.remediation: Create a hooks configuration (.cursor/hooks.json, .claude/settings.json hooks key, .devin/hooks.v1.json event map, or .devin/config.json hooks key) — hooks are the harness layer that can observe and control the agent loop deterministically.

checks.title: Hook events and handlers are structurally valid
checks.evidence: hooks/hooks.json: events: PreToolUse, PreCompact, SessionStart, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd.
checks.remediation: Declare at least one structurally valid hook event and every metadata field required by your tool; unrecognized future events are reported as warnings.

checks.title: Gate hook guards risky operations
checks.evidence: Gate hook(s) registered on: PreToolUse.
checks.remediation: Register a gate hook (Cursor: beforeShellExecution / beforeMCPExecution / preToolUse / beforeReadFile; Claude Code or Devin: PreToolUse / PermissionRequest) that guards destructive operations.

checks.title: Feedback hook observes agent output
checks.evidence: Feedback hook(s) registered on: PostToolUse, Stop.
checks.remediation: Register a feedback hook (Cursor: afterFileEdit / postToolUse / stop; Claude Code: PostToolUse; Devin: PostToolUse / Stop) — e.g. auto-format edited files or run a quick lint.
